Short Version - XCOM: Enemy Unknown and Enemy Within are vastly superior to this game. Go buy them instead, or if you have them and want more Firaxis XCOM, install and play the Long War mod.
I wanted to like this game so bad. Hundreds of hours into Enemy Unknown and I was ready and raring to go for the next step. And there are certainly next steps in XCOM 2, the Starting concealment, the changes to Psionics, different enemy types, those were all really good ideas. On the other hand, there's simply too many things that can make your game go sideways through literally no fault of your own. In EU, I usually knew when I made a mistake. Sometimes things go poorly one turn, and that's the way it is, and it usually doesn't happen too often unless you're just committed to riding the bullet train of bad decisions. XCOM 2 just is the bullet train of failure, and there's no brakes on that train.
Barring the DLC, the art is slick and totally on point, a really good iteration of Enemy Unknown's style. Tygen is cool, but lacks the personality and interest of Vahlen. He's 24/7 cool as a cucumber, and is just constantly aloof, where Vahlen had a proper forward face, but there were plenty of hints through dialogue that at any given time she was basically 2 seconds away from dissecting the nearest thing to her, living or dead, while singing opera. Lily Shen's interest basically drops right after her introduction, she never develops even though she's got the most opportunity to do so. On top of that, she looks EXACTLY like Jackie Ma from Sleeping Dogs, right down to the hairdo and freckles, so that's wierd.
The soldier base models are all basically flat, they have zero silhouette and really wierd proportions. Even though there's more customization, somehow it feels more constrained, and I think it's due to there just being less interesting faces and hairdos available.
And, once again (see: Batman: Arkham Knight), XCOM 2 has massive performance issues by trying to ship a "next-gen" game on a decade-old engine.
Like Rocksteady, they bolted too many custom tools and rendering software onto Unreal Engine 3, and while Unreal is a fantastic engine, they both were trying to do rendering that the engine was just not meant to do. So, came the litany of "I have a top-end machine and I get 20 FPS" and "Game crashes at launch" on forums, and while I only had catastrophic issues once or twice, the load times and frame chug just inside the Skyranger are simply unforgivable.
The story of XCOM losing was a bitter pill to swallow, but it gave a good start to why there's more aliens in the future. But beyond that, the presentation just lacks the same punch as Enemy Unknown. It lacks tension and a sense of urgency, even though that's what XCOM 2 is supposed to be completely centered around.
I'll go watch the intro cinematic to Enemy Unknown just to watch it, because it gets me totally jazzed up to save the world. Michael McCann kills it with the music, and that stutter cut with the Skyranger gets me giddier than a schoolgirl to go shoot some aliens. On the other hand,the intro to XCOM 2 has scenes that should arguably be even more intense, but the lackluster directing, the totally midtone soundwork, it all made it feel so.... ordinary. Like blowing up ADVENT checkpoints is just what you do on a Tuesday afternoon. Though, Bradford jumping through a window was pretty sweet.
The sense of tedium never goes away, as you're constantly shifting back and forth across zones because everything takes too long. You'll rarely finish one activity before you have to go do a guerilla op, oh did you happen to notice, ADVENT's  putting the boots to some hippies in a commune that happen to be our friends, hey you should go look at this wierd spot we found, oh by the way, you need to go pick up your monthly cheque from this spot because we couldn't be arsed to mail it to you direct, and there's a 3 day processing wait, did you want to sell stuff, well you gotta go fly there too, because apparently there's only ONE Black Market bazaar on the planet.
There's a nice balance that Enemy Unknown struck between the Strategy and Tactical layers of their game, The Tactical portion was an overt stress-fest of playing hide-and-seek with bullets, doing Hail Marys behind the tiny log that is your only available cover, and hoping to Sweet Baby Ray's that the Meld canister you're after isn't just a total pod-fest of X-rays. The Strategy layer was much more subtle, and the contrast makes the game actually playable. The Strategy layer gives you time to think, to manage your resources and marshal your thoughts on your game plan. It can be a good 10 minutes before another mission crops up, which is good downtime for the player so they aren't keyed up for too long.
XCOM 2 learned nothing from its predecessor. The constantly running around, the Doom Ticker front and center, everything takes too long, and missions pop up with an annoying frequency to how much you can actually get done in the Strategy layer before "Hey, you gotta pop half-way round the world to go save those dirty hippies again" There's really never time to rest in XCOM 2 and it's frankly exhausting even thinking about booting the game up.
The last sticking point, and really the final straw for me, is really how screwed the game balance was, and continues to be. Instead of say, fixing the fact that missions play like a round of "Whose Line is it Anyway?", where the shot percentages are made up and the aiming angles don't matter, they decide a good idea is to heavily nerf one of the only options for consistent damage, and taking away the biggest reason you pick Volatile Mix (increased grenade radius). Not even mentioning removing the only means of stopping "Run-n-Gun" Chrysallids and Stun Lancers. And there was obviously decisions that were made akin to those bouts of insanity throughout its development. Tons of enemies have armour (DR in EU) and Shieldbearers can give anyone in a huge radius armour, fine. But they took out Shredder rounds, so the only ways are, Psyhic attacks on non-robotic enemies (which bypasses armour, so the rest of your squad is still stuck in DR hell), an extremely high-level perk for Rangers, and the aforementioned nerfed grenades. Thin Men made a new appearance as the Vipers, and they can strangle you from a distance, great! But, (up until a patch a couple weeks ago, where they can't dodge 100% shots anymore), they have a high chance to straight-up ignore half of incoming damage from any weapon that rolls to hit. Your squad starts most missions Concealed, which allows you to try and get the jump on your enemy by (potentially) setting up kill zones to obliterate a pod before they can shoot back, Awesome! But why is there a 10, or even better, a FIVE (yes, five) turn timer on the mission? It completely nullifies the concept of Concealment and geurilla warfare if your only option to succeed in the mission is to dash forward non-stop until you reach the objective, because you WILL run into a pod, you WILL lose Concealment, and after that, you can't hope to just keep running and expect to win.
There's things to like in XCOM 2, but it's just such an unfun, buggy mess.

Half life.The game that started it all.Even though it was made back in 1998,it is still a gem.I don't vote games by their graphics,but by their gameplay.This was an immersing,wonderful and addicting experience for me.I lived another life.In this game.The game has everything a gamer asks for: Immersing Gameplay,Indulging story,A Nice Selection of Weapons,and graphics that were thrilling in the year it was made,but are all old now.Even now this title holds up till today,shining its glory as the first game that Valve ever made,and a game that changed Gaming itself.Now I will have a look at the main aspects of a good game.
WARNING: A little bit of spoiling ahead.
Gameplay: Excellent.Either you are blasting monsters from an alternate dimension or just trying to pick off those squad men who just don't seem to put you in peace.There were a few places where it did get a little bit boring,but that was because I couldn't wait until I would experience something new.The terrain in the game is nicely made,even though it is pretty old due to the date it was made.The places you travel through are pretty different,you won't be bored of seeing the same old place over and over again.The game itself is nicely balanced;except that they could have put less ammo in the game,so you wouldn't always have a gun loaded. 9/10
Story: A nice story is told throughout the game,and that is guaranteed to keep you hooked until the last moment of the game.Even though it doesn't have any cutscenes,it tells its story just wonderfully.It keeps you in first person mode all of the time,so it makes you "live" the character all the way through the story.All the stuff that is happening in the game seems kind of logical,as if could happen in real life.The characters are well done as well,for they act as normal people would act.They are as they should be,they speak,fight,help you and do other stuff.And there is a wierdly acting character which stands out in the game;but I will let you figure that out for yourself.There aren't the same scientists all over and over again,but we can't say this with security guards.The enemies are widely assorted and won't make you think that they are dumb,but play as they are real and trying to get you.No dull moment will get you in this game,so don't be afraid of experiencing any in this game.  10/10
Weapons: There is a wide assort of weapons to fit you in this game,but do not expect too much.There are the main weapons you would except from a game like this,and maybe a little bit more due to an "Monster Invasion" going on all around you.The game has its own signature weapon: A Crowbar.But that is also the only melee weapon that you can use in this game.While you progress through the game you will find weapons,but there aren't many,so every weapon you get,you make use of,because all of them are unique.As I won't spoil much here,I will just tell you that there are weapons from the pistol even to such weapons like a rocket launcher,and a few of alien techologies are found in the game as well.You will find yourself exploring all around you to get some ammo for your favourite weapon,because it gives you tons of ammo for a wide selection of weapons,and the ammo that you need may not be findable anywhere.When you shoot a gun it feels like you shoot a gun,meaning that you will find the gun bouncing back in your hand when you shoot it,and you can hear the sound for gun firing is well done as well.But when shooting a rocket launcher you will not bounce back,but if you move while shooting it the rocket will go wrong and hit another spot,depending on which way you moved.Even if you don't have any ammo,you get to use a alien techonlogy which has unlimited ammo.Even though it recharges over time,it doesn't take much of it and it has special abilities.  8.5/10
Enemies: From the headcrab even to the final boss,the enemies are nicely balanced.You are slowly introduced to each enemy and its tactics,so you know what to use on it and what to do.You probably won't find yourself facing a unnormally big army of enemies if you aren't well armed.Once you learn the tactics the enemies use it is easy to defeat them,just keep a look out for them,or otherwise you might find yourself in quite a pickle.I wouldn't say that the enemies are hard.You can use the terrain to your advantage as well.Luckily,one group of your enemies is fighting another,so you can use that to your advantage as well,if you find the right moment.*wink*.But I wouldn't rely on such stuff,I would just get myself a nice arsenal of weapons and go defeat that crowd of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.There are a few weapons which have unlimited ammo,and I feel that is unbalanced.Don't go prancing around as a pony as well,you will get your♥♥♥♥♥kicked.There are flying enemies,crawling enemies,walking enemies and big enemies.The crawling ones are easy,just keep a look out for them so they don't get the jump on you.The Flying ones need the right weapons,like a zoom in crossbow,for they fly around and shoot at you and when you get close to them they just fly away.The walking ones are easy enough,just keep a shotgun on your hand and you will be OK.But the big ones need a plan,a strategy and a assault of weapons. 9.5/10
Graphics: From Black Mesa labs to even Alien fields of doom,this game is amazing.It now has its own HD models,so a few things look better when the models are turned "ON".Any computer will be able to get this game running,so why not jump in it already?And as this game was made in 1998,don't expect modern graphics.But that couldn't stop you from playing this game,could it?The terrain is kind of blocky and the characters as well,but if you look past that point get ready to indulge into a game that made gaming as it is today.And the graphics aren't that bad,everything is quite understandable.They have made the graphics the best way they could,and I don't blame them because I don't vote a game by its graphics.And if you can't stand the graphics there is a Source version of the game,made by Valve as well.There is a version made by fans as well,but I wouldn't recommend that because it is modified a bit.But the original is the best in my opinion as it is the completly unmodified version of half life,and the best out there.Of course,that is if you look past the graphics.There are even little details specified in the originl game,but they won't be seen so good and will be kind of blurred.But be sure to keep your eyes lit,for there are many levers,buttons and things like that throughout the game,that blend in with the enviroment. 8.5/10
Overall look: Even though this game is dated,it is definently not dead.Be sure to pick this game up on a sale,or even buy it at its full price,because this game is worth every cent you pay for it.I loved the game,it really got me pulled in and the story was just stunning.I loved every place I came upon to in this game,seeking new adventure and traveling on into the deep unknown.This game is filled with interesting moments and is guaranteed to keep you aroused until the very ending.This is a great classic and everyone should play it,it is an experience not to be missed.It changed gaming as it is now,and was a hit in gaming and it still is.A wonderful game. FINAL SCORE ::::::::: 9/10.

Warning: This review is a bit more crude and shallow than most of the ones I post, but we ARE talking about Bayonetta here, so here goes.
The game runs perfectly. The cutscenes are at 30FPS but the game itself is 60FPS like everyone says. It's smooth as butter with a 360 controller, but you can grab the mouse for tricky aiming sequences (like the arcade minigame) and that works fine too.
I first decided to pick this game up after seeing Anita Sarkeesian's video saying how offensive it was, and I was not disappointed. I'm never on a console though, I'm always on my PC, so when I saw this get released on Steam I almost jumped out of my seat!
Don't ask me about the storyline. It does have dialogue, some of the cutscenes are like motion comics, and some are fully animated. It's something about angels vs. demons, lost memories, revenge, I have no idea. But what I do know is the action is great. Combos are easy to pull off; you can just mash buttons and crank the left stick and you'll end up looking awesome. Most people recommend playing on harder difficulty, which forces you to dodge and master your combos. I just play on easy mode since I'm only here for the eye candy.
There's also an upgrade system where you can purchase perks and abilities with a currency that drops off fallen enemies. This currency, by the way, looks like all the ones Sonic the Hedgehog missed during his adventures. There are a few light puzzles, but mostly it's just kicking♥♥♥♥♥and looking good.

I'm copying and pasting this review from one I wrote seven years ago, for my college-at-the-time's paper, the Corsair! Be aware that there may be spoilers, though they're all my observations from, as I say, a quarter-way through the game. A small update in that for PC, the game has been upgraded and locked at 60 frames per second, supporting 4K resolutions and, for a limited time, coming with digital deluxe content for free including digital artbook, soundtrack sample and avatars.
-----
Bayonetta
by SEGA and Platinum Games
Players: 1
Genre: Third-person action
Rating: Mature for blood and gore, intense violence, partial nudity, strong language, suggestive themes
Release 1/05/10
-----
One genre of video games that I didn't really think I'd be into is the twitch action genre; in this genre, the player must make split-second decisions to ensure his survival. My coordination doesn't usually allow me to enjoy those games, but in rare cases a game breaks through the mold and keeps me interested. Hideki Kamiya, maker of two of my favorite game series, Devil May Cry and Resident Evil, has again brought hope to my reflexes with Bayonetta.
The protagonist in this game is the eponymous Bayonetta, a 500-plus year old witch (not looking a day over 25) risen after a civil war between her clan, the Umbra Witches and their rivals, the Lumen Sages, sent her into a long slumber in a coffin at the bottom of a lake. This witch, like others of her kind, has made contracts with unholy forces; the rules of her world state that because of this, she is condemned to Inferno. This also means that once she rises, she is the target of myriad attacks from the angels of Paradiso, who keep trying to send her where they feel she belongs. Fortunately, her compatriots are never far behind her; in fact, they're in her hair.
Bayonetta's 'costume,' ostensibly shiny black leather, is actually cleverly manipulated hair, which she also uses to summon forth her infernal allies, in a technique known as the Wicked Weave. She uses this technique to send those angels foolhardy enough to confront her, which are not necessarily beautiful in form, packing back to Paradiso. She wants the companion piece to her large medallion which she always wears; together forming the Eyes of the World, a quarter of the way through the story, they seem to be a MacGuffin, a plot device the functioning of which is not important but serves as the impetus for the journey.
Bayonetta often finds herself in the city of Vigrid; There, she's been told, are clues to restore her faded memory. Vigrid is crowded with people; however, they don't see her, and we only see their shadows, because Bayonetta is almost always in Purgatorio, the parallel dimension in which she fights the angels who try to kill her, and she cannot interfere in their affairs.
Aiding Bayonetta on her journey is her bumbling underworld contact, comic relief Enzo, as well as Samuel L. Jackson wannabe, bald, trash-talking arms dealer, Rodin. Against her, amongst the many angels, are the four representations of the Cardinal Virtues; they take the form of epic boss battles at the end of every quarter of the game, and her main rival Jeanne, the possessor of the other Eye of the World, shows up to harass her at several points.
The game has a very music-and-candy-oriented slant; Bayonetta bounces and whirls hypnotically through her attacks, and cutscenes showing off her dancing abilities are common. CDs (or pieces of them) acquired from mini-bosses may be redeemed at Rodin's for new weapons, and many of the items Bayonetta uses for recovery or augmentation take the form of lollipops or other confections.
The entire game does not really take itself seriously, from its storyline to its flippant yet alluring protagonist and solid supporting cast. The combat is satisfying, the story ridiculously cheesy, and the visuals great. The only minor gripe I may have about the game is that the camera often focuses on the latest and greatest spectacle, of which there are many, rather on what I need it to focus on, namely the ground around Bayonetta and where I need to go next. This doesn't stop me from giving the game five out of five stars.

Enter the action of a stunning new MMO Shooter where you can make the difference on the battlefield.
Customize your set up with a huge range of weapons to suit your play style.
Enjoy different game modes and use your class skills to pulverize your enemies.
Black Squad is a stunning new game where you get to decide the fate of the world. Will you let the chaos of the Viper Circle rule or stop them as a Peacemaker? Here your skills on the battlefield will make the difference in a fast paced action MMO FPS.
When you play you have a tutorial showing you how to play and showing off some of the more unique aspects of the game. Once you complete this you are given a set of weapons and then taken to the main screen where you can customise your loadout as well as get access to the store to buy more guns.
There are 4 classes available to play, where you can use unique skills in some of the battle modes. The classes are: Assault, Recon, Command and Support. Each of these has its own unique skills that can really make a difference. From a field aid kit for an ally to an air support bombing run there are lots of options for you.
There are also several styles of game for you, the classic Team Deathmatch is here as well as a Demolition level where you have to blow up or defend a position. There is a Destruction level where you need to destroy as many buildings as you can while stopping the enemy. Finally we have an Assassination game where you have to attack or defend an NPC target.
Before you enter these games you can customize your loadout of weapons, here you can browse the shop for a variety of weapon classes such as SMG’s, Assault Rifles and Sniper Rifles. Once you have them you can set up 3 different pre game options and you select the one you want before each battle.
The game uses several currencies: Gold, BScoins, Medals and Bullets. Gold and Medals are earned in the game and Bullets are the real money premium currency. Bullets allow you to buy weapon crates that contain 1 of several items and a few BScoins (which can be used to get specific guns in the store).
The gameplay here is pretty fast paced, but is also well balanced. A sniper can still one shot you but most of the time you have a fighting chance based on your gear. This leaves it down to your reactions and skills in the battlefield, and that’s a pretty nice place to be right now.
Using the Unreal engine Black Squad has a pretty good look to it too. The gameplay is smooth and it looks great. There are lots of custom options for the ui and graphics while you are in the game too. The sound effects also match and compliment the game well so it adds up to a fun experience.
Overall there is a lot of positive stuff about Black Squad, the game is enjoyable and there is a growing community and player base. Here you have a nice mix of options and gameplay that make for enough action to keep you going. A great game with a lot of positives and a bright future.

Drop Alive is a bit of a mixed bag, but woth checking out for free.
Pros:
*Hand-drawn artwork and animation lend the game a plesant storybook feel. The squishy water droplet is totes adorbs.
*The  concept and mechanics of the water shrinking, as well as changing form to steam and ice are imaginative and fantastic (when they work).
*Soundtrack is nice and unobtrusive-- I'd actually like an option to download the soundtrack and listen to it by itself.
Cons:
*Several reviewers have compared Drop Alive to Super Meat Boy, and although I understand the comparison (because of the frequent deaths), it doesn't hold up as well.
*It's a bit slow paced for the type of platformer it is; it's not puzzly enough (for my tastes) to be as slow as it is.
*Its controls are nowhere near as tight as those in SMB, and a lot of the collisions seem off. Sometimes, for example, spikes will kill you, but sometimes you can stand on them like a platform. Sometimes the drop jumps right when you want him to, but sometimes he just sort of schluffs along, to his doom. In a platformer-- especially one with so much death-- precision is key, and Drop Alive just isn't there.
*Which leads me to my final criticism-- the rage factor. Unfair feeling deaths made this game more frustrating than fun, which is at direct odds with the game's cute/relaxing aesthetic.
So come for the artwork and the concept, not for the gameplay. If that sounds like something you'd like (and I can think of worse ways to spend 45 minutes or so), give it a shot.

The most satisfying thing about Dark Souls 3 is that feeling of personal achievement you get when accomplishing a certain goal. Whether it's discovering a hidden room that only your curiosity as a player could've helped you find, or outwitting a group of enemies in a blade dance until the death, only to be put in your place by that most irrelevant enemy ever that you've slain and it's whole family half a dozen times in the last 20 minutes. Degrading, I know, but this game really does a good job at making each of it's enemies noticed and threatening. Dark Souls 3 just does things that make you feel appreciated as a player that put time in to learn the game.
Most games have a channeled experience, where only a certain amount of attention and skill is required to progress, therefore limiting replay value. Whereas Dark Souls 3 rewards and caters to a large variety of playstyles, and certain playstyles can change the difficulty drastically. Want to use a whacky challenge build with that new pokey weapon you found? - Sure thing! - Want to just go in blind and play the game naturally, experiencing the atmosphere without focusing on any specific playstyle (maybe even silently enjoying the constant struggle of a game known for it's brutality whilst doing so?) - I say do it! - Or maybe you fancy playing with others and destroying everything in your path? - It's all there to experience! - Gosh, even playing the anti-hero is fun. Showing those basic knight bi****s where to go when they enter your domain is like child's play (Just don't forget the etiquette and bow before you destroy them for heaven's sake!)
10/10 would play again, and I did! In a shiny New Game Plus :)
PS: Pointing down is a symbol of good fortune, so don't feel too bad when it happens to you... #Feels

I'm going to give Fractured Space a cautious recommendation as it is still a very early alpha. It's a very playable alpha, granted, but there's still a lot of very basic features missing.
The good:
+Ships feel different and handle like capital ships of great size.
+Abilities and placement are important.
+Crew setup, upgrades and team comp feels important and has a lot of depth.
+Games are long, but always feel rewarding.
+Ships look great and the graphics are overall pretty good.
The bad:
-Some very basic things are missing like filtering for servers and the options to make a party.
-The UI presentation is confusing and is a little too minimal, there's a lot of information that's easy to miss.
-Expect ships and abilities to be over/under-powered. I personally had a lot of trouble with the Sniper ships, as of right now.
-Very few players, except during free weekends.
-You have to grind to unlock new abilities and ships, unless you buy in-game currency.
-The music is quite lackluster.
Bottom Line:
If you're itching to step onto the bridge and command your own ship into battle then Fractured Space will certainly scratch that spot, but bear in mind that it's still alpha and the game still needs more work.
October 2015 update:
The game just got a huge update which has vastly improved the crew mechanics and seems to have balanced out the different ships far more. Snipers seem to have been reworked, thank god. Furthermore, we have a new game mode that is shorter and more action packed, but it is possible to base rush which can lead to some games feeling cheesy. I would still make this a cautious recommendation, but with the knowledge that the game is improving.
November 2015 update:
Another big update just released and with it a much needed 2 part tutorial to help new players learn the basics of the game. You can now also freely choose between the two game modes. For the next update I would love to see more options for the ship abilities and more new crew to choose from, especially a Gunnery Technician that could increase your turret turn rate.
January 2016 update:
Matchmaking has been released and it's now possible to party up, before searching for a match, however it's only possible to party up with one friend so far. The tech tree has been reworked and so has the tutorial. The 30 % faster respawn time granted to teams with a disconnected player is not enough and should include a minor stat buff. Finally, for the next update I would really like to see more crew and more loadout options for the existing ships.

A follow up to the 2'nd Age of Empires that everyone loved.
Among many this game is not so good, some things were simplified, such as gathering resources - now there are 3 instead of 4 of them and your villagers don't have to come back to the lumberjack or the city centre to store them.

It's a shame that there weren't any additional elements added to the Steam release of the game.
Controls being one of the more touchy ones. For instance, to change the hotkeys you need to manually go through each tab. There is also no Steam Cloud, but they did add Trading Cards so that's one interesting thing to look forward to.
This game is soon to have 10 years after it's release. But this edition is by far the best one yet. You get all the expansions. Working multiplayer with a community that still lives. And of course that same old strategy many remember and honor as "one of the best".
The modest presentation of it's ancestors passed away. I'd say that the magnificence of the soundtrack itself says a lot:
A Musical score composed by Ensemble Studios musicians Stephen Rippy and Kevin McMullan.
If History is of any interest to you, if the New World conquests were something you're keen on. Buy this game, especially when on sale!

Half life.The game that started it all.Even though it was made back in 1998,it is still a gem.I don't vote games by their graphics,but by their gameplay.This was an immersing,wonderful and addicting experience for me.I lived another life.In this game.The game has everything a gamer asks for: Immersing Gameplay,Indulging story,A Nice Selection of Weapons,and graphics that were thrilling in the year it was made,but are all old now.Even now this title holds up till today,shining its glory as the first game that Valve ever made,and a game that changed Gaming itself.Now I will have a look at the main aspects of a good game.
WARNING: A little bit of spoiling ahead.
Gameplay: Excellent.Either you are blasting monsters from an alternate dimension or just trying to pick off those squad men who just don't seem to put you in peace.There were a few places where it did get a little bit boring,but that was because I couldn't wait until I would experience something new.The terrain in the game is nicely made,even though it is pretty old due to the date it was made.The places you travel through are pretty different,you won't be bored of seeing the same old place over and over again.The game itself is nicely balanced;except that they could have put less ammo in the game,so you wouldn't always have a gun loaded. 9/10
Story: A nice story is told throughout the game,and that is guaranteed to keep you hooked until the last moment of the game.Even though it doesn't have any cutscenes,it tells its story just wonderfully.It keeps you in first person mode all of the time,so it makes you "live" the character all the way through the story.All the stuff that is happening in the game seems kind of logical,as if could happen in real life.The characters are well done as well,for they act as normal people would act.They are as they should be,they speak,fight,help you and do other stuff.And there is a wierdly acting character which stands out in the game;but I will let you figure that out for yourself.There aren't the same scientists all over and over again,but we can't say this with security guards.The enemies are widely assorted and won't make you think that they are dumb,but play as they are real and trying to get you.No dull moment will get you in this game,so don't be afraid of experiencing any in this game.  10/10
Weapons: There is a wide assort of weapons to fit you in this game,but do not expect too much.There are the main weapons you would except from a game like this,and maybe a little bit more due to an "Monster Invasion" going on all around you.The game has its own signature weapon: A Crowbar.But that is also the only melee weapon that you can use in this game.While you progress through the game you will find weapons,but there aren't many,so every weapon you get,you make use of,because all of them are unique.As I won't spoil much here,I will just tell you that there are weapons from the pistol even to such weapons like a rocket launcher,and a few of alien techologies are found in the game as well.You will find yourself exploring all around you to get some ammo for your favourite weapon,because it gives you tons of ammo for a wide selection of weapons,and the ammo that you need may not be findable anywhere.When you shoot a gun it feels like you shoot a gun,meaning that you will find the gun bouncing back in your hand when you shoot it,and you can hear the sound for gun firing is well done as well.But when shooting a rocket launcher you will not bounce back,but if you move while shooting it the rocket will go wrong and hit another spot,depending on which way you moved.Even if you don't have any ammo,you get to use a alien techonlogy which has unlimited ammo.Even though it recharges over time,it doesn't take much of it and it has special abilities.  8.5/10
Enemies: From the headcrab even to the final boss,the enemies are nicely balanced.You are slowly introduced to each enemy and its tactics,so you know what to use on it and what to do.You probably won't find yourself facing a unnormally big army of enemies if you aren't well armed.Once you learn the tactics the enemies use it is easy to defeat them,just keep a look out for them,or otherwise you might find yourself in quite a pickle.I wouldn't say that the enemies are hard.You can use the terrain to your advantage as well.Luckily,one group of your enemies is fighting another,so you can use that to your advantage as well,if you find the right moment.*wink*.But I wouldn't rely on such stuff,I would just get myself a nice arsenal of weapons and go defeat that crowd of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.There are a few weapons which have unlimited ammo,and I feel that is unbalanced.Don't go prancing around as a pony as well,you will get your♥♥♥♥♥kicked.There are flying enemies,crawling enemies,walking enemies and big enemies.The crawling ones are easy,just keep a look out for them so they don't get the jump on you.The Flying ones need the right weapons,like a zoom in crossbow,for they fly around and shoot at you and when you get close to them they just fly away.The walking ones are easy enough,just keep a shotgun on your hand and you will be OK.But the big ones need a plan,a strategy and a assault of weapons. 9.5/10
Graphics: From Black Mesa labs to even Alien fields of doom,this game is amazing.It now has its own HD models,so a few things look better when the models are turned "ON".Any computer will be able to get this game running,so why not jump in it already?And as this game was made in 1998,don't expect modern graphics.But that couldn't stop you from playing this game,could it?The terrain is kind of blocky and the characters as well,but if you look past that point get ready to indulge into a game that made gaming as it is today.And the graphics aren't that bad,everything is quite understandable.They have made the graphics the best way they could,and I don't blame them because I don't vote a game by its graphics.And if you can't stand the graphics there is a Source version of the game,made by Valve as well.There is a version made by fans as well,but I wouldn't recommend that because it is modified a bit.But the original is the best in my opinion as it is the completly unmodified version of half life,and the best out there.Of course,that is if you look past the graphics.There are even little details specified in the originl game,but they won't be seen so good and will be kind of blurred.But be sure to keep your eyes lit,for there are many levers,buttons and things like that throughout the game,that blend in with the enviroment. 8.5/10
Overall look: Even though this game is dated,it is definently not dead.Be sure to pick this game up on a sale,or even buy it at its full price,because this game is worth every cent you pay for it.I loved the game,it really got me pulled in and the story was just stunning.I loved every place I came upon to in this game,seeking new adventure and traveling on into the deep unknown.This game is filled with interesting moments and is guaranteed to keep you aroused until the very ending.This is a great classic and everyone should play it,it is an experience not to be missed.It changed gaming as it is now,and was a hit in gaming and it still is.A wonderful game. FINAL SCORE ::::::::: 9/10.

I have never written a review for any game before, but I felt that this one was definitely worth my time and effort. That being said, here's my review...
I liked Terraria, and I played it relentlessly until I got all the stuff I wanted and then sorta lost interest. Starbound seems to be full of endless possibilities, and it's only in the beta state! I can't wait for the next update to this game so I can explore farther reaches of the universe and take on new bosses to be able to craft all new sorts of stuff!! PLUS the amount of vanity item (furniture, apparel, etc...) is awesome! allowing me to create a completely unique home that I'm actually HAPPY to return to. Minecraft and Terraria couldn't really nail that for me. Although sometimes it gets frustrating with the amount of Pixels (in-game currency) lost for each death. I had 5800, died and was left with 3200. That death toll is slightly exorbidant. Something I would HIGHLY recommend is, the second you get into a new sector, get the required materials for the new armors set(s) unlocked at the crafting table. It will save you grief. Also carry a tent to sleep in when your health is low. I would recommend getting on with the Early Access so:
A: You can support the development so we recieve the best possible final product.
B: You get to enjoy the game right now, and every update from here on is like christmas and makes you go "ooh! new stuff!"
C: You don't have to pay the full release price, that I'm guessing will be about $25.00. So that saves you $10 and you get to enjoy a great game right now!

Hmmm what to say about starbound, well first off i'm going to make this clear. I don't mean in any way to insult the developers of this game, this review will only state my honest opinion about that game at
Now thats out of the way it's time to begin.
This next part is kind of first experice and first thoughts, skip it if you want to get to my opinion as of now
So, starbound, an early access game that I thought of as being "Terraria in space." I had played terraria a lot with friends before buying this game and loved terraria, so I assumed that this would be the next terraria. A friend of mine had bought the game and I had watched him play it a bit, everything looked awesome, from the tools he had to the things he did, I was convinced. I bought this game at its full price at the time, which was 15 dollars and started to install and play. The gameplay seemed odd and clunky and unfinished, but i convinced myself it was fine and played on with my friends. I then put the game down for probably 4 months. I finally started playing again around may.
Ok now on to my opinion now
I came back to the game thinking it would be completely different in terms of new content, being away from and still growing game for 4 month you would expect that. I found the game nearly identical to how it last was, it felt odd and unfinished. Me and another friend had the same feeling towards the game and compared it to terraria. Now terraria has a fun, not very complicated feel to it, you can get into the game in minutes. Now starbound on the other hand I had a hard time getting used to, I knew about the game and how to play, just playing it wasn't enjoyable.
I'm not sure how to explain it but it just was not fun to play at its current state, it was odd, seemingly unfinished and just overall weird. Because of that I can not recommend this game at its current state.
Edit: So I wanna add some things that I forgot. This game has some potential, If we get updates more and with more content this game could live up to its "Terraria in space" image. I think this game could be salvaged but I feel due to the amount of negetive reviews, they have lost most of their current player base, unless it is slavaged, they lost me as well.

Bethesda is lost. I used to love this company and it used to be my drive I held onto when I was first learning how to make games. I looked up to Bethesda as a role model, and as the standard for a lot of video game devs out there... But now I see that they don't care about me, or any of their playerbase for that matter. Bethesda has gone back on a lot of promises and at this point I am done with them outright... First they release a game that is expansive, but shallow. Huge, yet empty. An RPG with no actual choices. It is a bad joke of itself. It has some redeeming elements but it is far from what the series used to be. On release they said there would never be any paid mods. Then Bethesda refuses to put out review copies of their games, which is downright infuriating. Why would you not give your games the free publicity it deserves? Do you not trust your game to make statements on their own? If your game cannot stand to criticism then it shouldn't. Then the company decides what the people really want is ANOTHER re-release of Skyrim... We don't want it. Stop pushing it. At what point does the company finally realize that I don't want Skyrim for my hairdryer and would instead love another shot at making an elder scrolls game with a world that actually feels alive. Nothing in their last 2 games feel responsive. Nothing I ever do in these games will ever feel impactful because theres always another radiant quest to point me at a settlement I have to clear or another house I have to steal from. I refuse to make my own story, I refuse to pay a company for the same game 4 times, I refuse to allow Bethesda to walk over its playerbase with a joke of a paid mod release, after claiming that very thing would not happen.
I realize that this review is inclusive of Bethesda as well as Fallout 4, but they are both equally important, I am immensley dissapointed in Bethesda as a fan. I hope one day they can prove themselves worthy of the love I have given them to this point.

I truly love this game.  It's poetic, adrenaline-pumping, masochistic, and brilliant.  Your successes are clawed out of its grip by tooth and nail -- Darkest Dungeon constantly pushes you to the edge, and then shoves you right over it.  The rush of uncertainty, risk harrying at your heels, and nervous exhilaration drive the experience.  Every party excursion is a deep gamble no matter how you try to prepare.  The ladder toward greater challenges becomes more compelling the more you climb.  I gush about this game to everyone I know.
Another thing I like about DD is that it features a pretty even mix of women and men as NPCs and class archetypes.  The devs chose to make this normal in the game's setting.  The result is like eating beef from happy cows -- zero guilt and a better flavor.
Be ready for:
- Balancing that throws the player into hell and pulls no punches (Even Dark Souls is "designed for success" more than this, if you ask me)
- Some of the most satisfying voice-over narration I've enjoyed in any game
- Permadeath that cuts deeply on a strategic and psychological level
- Resource famine forcing tough decisions with no clear best answers
- Planning for "the long run" as RNG plays a role at every turn (this is an asset -- heightens the suspense, player's sense of vulnerability, and demand for flexible strategy)
- Thick-as-molasses atmosphere of Poe/Lovecraft macabre
- Wild swings between victory and crippling failure
Do yourself a favor and invest in this masterpiece if you're at all a fan of the genres it's tagged in!
My advice: choose "Darkest" difficulty for your first file, and avoid mechanics spoilers.  Going in blind makes it more exciting and rewarding.

I saw this in my library and decided to give it a go. I only played two games, but even still, I was able to do something as a starter nooby with nothing. In the second, I tried an attack ship and got 6 kills (as level 1 vs lvls 6-13). In that sense, it's pretty balanced, I'd say (compared to other games where you join as a new player and get decimated and can do nothing).
When I first got on, there were only two servers with players. One had 10/10, the other had 1/10. I was a little discouraged, but I joined the open server anyways and played a game. Afterwards, there were like 6 servers with players and it started growing, which caught me by surprise. I think more people should play this game :P
I, for one, plan on playing this more. (Few more details down below)
As some others have said, it's a team game. I had no idea what I was doing but figured out how to work with others, at least. When I was a little support ship getting hammered by a huge enemy ship, a bigger allied ship came in between us and soaked up the damage. I healed it up and we won against 2 others. In the second game I played, it looked like the whole enemy team didn't care about their team composition and played whatever they wanted. That costed them the win. Our team had a mix of attackers, supports, and a heavy. Theirs? I believe most of them were attack ships and there was maybe 1 heavy.
They say this when you get in the game, but because it's Alpha, there is no playable tutorial yet. However, they have a little video for you to watch that explains the controls and whatnot. That was enough to get me going at a decent pace. The rest, you learn as you go, I suppose.

OK, I'm going to give my input on this game one more time. It has changed a lot since I initially bought it in early access. I don't really get into number tweaks but some blatant obvious changes are still there. Like the adding of corpses, town events and two new hero classes as far as I'm aware. The corpses are stupid, they just drag out fights way longer than they need to be and that is not good in a game where the next attack against your hero could be fatal. The town events are cool, add some flavor to the town. And the Abomination, and trinket gypsy woman (I forgot her name.) are both interesting classes. The abomination being a front or second line bruiser, and the gypsy being a interesting support class.
Anyways, I love this game. The atmosphere, melancholy characters, and amazing artstyle. I'd say this game is way more than worth it if you enjoy heavy atmosphere and struggle in emotion in your characters. It makes the battles super dramatic and fun if you kind of get an idea of what your character would be like in a given situation. However, if emersion isn't your thing, then this game might not right for you. If you care more about the game as far as mechanics, it might be an annoying hassle. The Rng is pain, sometimes killing a super high leveled character without feeling like you could do anything about it, and on the opposite end, you could feel like your attacks never make contact. Then that leads to a painful grind of leveling up more characters only so they can get sent to their doom. That can certainly be aweful at times. That's why I think this game is better suited for small sessions, especially when you start to get into mid and late game. The game is a lot less aggrivating if you just stop playing when it starts making you angry. It's not worth getting frustrated over, it's supposed to be fun!
So if Rng and grind get on your nerves, and if you like long sessions in games. I don't think you'll like this game very much. However, if you love amazing atmosphere and unique monsters strait out eldritch fantasy and melancholy struggles with insanity then I think you'll adore this game. I myself, love the game no matter how annoying the mechanics become. It's very nice to play, and I personally would recommend it highly. I am merely saying that I understand people's complaints about the Rng and grind, cause they're defininitly real problems that could use some tweaking.

I first came upon this game by watching Markiplier play it one time. Having witnessed his unending frustration with it, I should have known what I was getting myself into when I decided to try it.
The first time was fun. The second, less fun. And it keeps going downhill from there.
The controls are absolutley infuriating and the music in the background only gets more annoying the longer you play. It's almost as if it's rubbing in your face that you haven't reached the toaster yet. Another thing that I hate is how the bread bounces off surfaces when rocking back and forth on one side... totally unnecessary and inaccurate to the laws of physics and freaking gravity. Also, just when you think it can't get worse, the camera completely screws you over so that you either have unneeded trouble seeing, or you can't see at all.
Loved the idea of this concept, but the mechanics are absolute crap. I'd like to meet someone who has been successful with this game and have them teach me their ways, because even as someone who is able to adapt very easily to different sets of controls, I had infinite amounts of trouble with this game.
Do not recommend this game- not for the easily-angered... although it would probably be enough to get the most patient of people yelling and screaming.

The game has a good support for input customisation, allowing players to hotkey unit control in many ways and provides rich realtime statistics for each selected unit and groups.
14 civilisations, including the two expansion packs (with Native and Asian civilisations), more than two thousand units, including combat units, buildings and nature stuff, create a realistic and very diverse world for anyone who wants to prove and improve their strategy skills.

So Starbound is a sandbox survival-adventure game. You collect items and weapons to survive as you traverse the universe in your personal spaceship.
Starbound is still in development, so it does have a few bugs here and there, but they're most definitely not common and usually don't effect gameplay severely. Starbound is very charming in its own way. It has many different mechanics, such as techs (items that improve the way your character moves, such as double jumps or quick dashes), that enhances the gameplay. The only problem I have with the game is that when you start off, it can be difficult to play due to the difficulty and lack of different supplies, but over time this issue fades as the game rewards your time and hard work with different items and weapons to help you along. Also the combat system is a bit awkward and hard to get used to, but over time I seemed to get used to it.
Overall I think Starbound is a fantastic game with tons of potential. I look forward to seeing it grow and shape into the great game it will be in the future.

I have read quite a few comments on here about Starbound. Some good, some bad, and some completely based around putting the game to the torch. To each their own, as I say, but in this instance I believe alot of the comments are based upon a lack of research, impatients, and an unwillingness to follow the developer's blog posts. I will tell you what I know of the game, and what I know of it's development, and from there you can form your opinion of it.
Part 1: The Game
Starbound is a Side Scrolling Open World, or rather Universe, Exploration game which is currently in beta. You travel from planet to planet discovering new biomes, resources, enemies, weapons, towns, etc. Each new game is randomly generated and completely unique. You fight bosses to move up to different sectors of space which have new resources, harder enemies, and better gear. Build homes, raid dungeons, explore new planets, and kill lots of space monsters is kind of the overall theme here. If you like Terraria or Sci-Fi (or both) this could be the game for you, but caution should also be taken. The game is not in the least bit finished, and alot of the current gameplay is merely frameworks or stand-ins for future updates (SEE PART 2 FOR MORE INFO).
Part 2: Development
The game is currently in beta, as the early access label says above. Some have accused this game to be a scam and others have claimed it to be garbage. What one needs to realize is that an early access game is just that, an early representation of what the overall release of the game will look like. Though, it is completely true what some have stated about the game. Some features feel, or are outright, broken. At a certain point, a lack of content is noticable. An update has not come out in a fairly long time. What these people won't tell you, however, is that the game is heavily in development. The team working on Starbound were, as I understand, moving to a new office abroad. Which slowed down development alot, but the team is at there new HQ and development has started again. The team posts blog posts on their page almost everyday to inform the ever waiting masses of the content they are currently working on, along with some fresh new screenshots of the new features.
Part 3: Impression
I really enjoyed playing Starbound for the longest time, but I have reached the point where I cannot seem to play it solely on the lack of content. I believe the programmers and designers still have alot of work ahead of them, but I see a very bright future for this game.

Before I write this review, let me give you a disclaimer. I've been playing this game a whole bunch and as a whole, I actually kind of liked it. Though it wasn't stellar as a Fallout game, it was a decent game in it's own right and could stand on it's merits.
This was before bethesda introduced it's horrendous "Creation Club" system.
The Creation Club is bethesda's way of trying to tap into the micro transaction market.
When it was introduced, the creation club promised curated premium mod content, painting a picture of high quality community made mods that were very close to DLC's in terms of scope. It was exciting because having a spot in the creation club meant that you had access to the tallent at bethesda during different phases of the development process. This was an unprecidented opportunity that was meant to push the modding community of not just fallout 4, but also skyrim, to new limits of content creation.
Fastfoward to the actual implementation of creation club. Do we get amazing DLC-esque quest content? Do we get loads of new and wacky gameplay systems, like changing seasons, moving dungeon platforms, and working spear combat?
No. We get cosmetic items. We get literal horse armor. We get the option to change our pipboys color scheme. What a letdown.
Also, to add injury to insult, my F4SE is broken. And it will keep breaking. Over and over again. because EVERY TIME BETHESDA WANTS TO UPDATE THE CREATION CLUB CONTENT, THEY WILL PATCH ALL OF IT TO YOUR COMPUTER, AND FORCE YOU TO DOWNLOAD 600+ MB's of DATA WITHOUT YOUR CONSENT.
They do this because, again, they want to cash in on microtransactions. They know that in order to circumvent the limitations of the PS4 and XBONE CONSOLES, they need to introduce these micrtransactions as a patch (official game), so that the people will have the opportunity to pay them a dollar to let them change their pip boys black. And they're too lazy to change it for the PC.
TL;DR
In Bethesda's latest iteration of their "Paid Mods" scheme, they somehow manage to turn a game into literal malware while simultaneously managing to completely destroy a large component of it's community modding tools (F4SE)

[Before you read this, take in to account that I still love this game with all my heart, and have cherished all the friends and experiences I have gained with this game. I will explain about those in this post too.]
Almost 900 Hours....
I loved playing this game. When the "No-Energy" Update came out, I played endlessly. There was so much content and stuff to do, I was addicted. I never stopped playing.
I couldn't stop. I loved the story, the gameplay, the heart and effort that went into every minute I played this game. But...
A few years later, things started to die down. And die down FAST. Even to the point where I was one of those people.
Lemme explain: No updates, Crown/Currency inflation, and constant grinding.
I'll start with the grinding. You can craft weapons and armor in this game. Its a known thing in MMO's, The materials are pretty easy to get, and crafting the item itself only needs a few k crowns, depending on the level/star of the item. But then you get to the "Alchemy Orbs"
OHHHHHHH BOY DO I HATE THESE THINGS WITH A BURNING PASSION. At first, it seems like your usual "Farm for this item" material. But what the game doesn't tell you, is that once you get an orb of a type, it has a "cooldown". Meaning, if you want to get some certain star type of orb, you'd have to farm for it. And we all know farming in video games is either really easy, or so hard you wanna pull your hairs out, 1 by 1. Once you finally get the orb(s) you wanted, you can't get any more. Exactly. You have to farm for the orb, and then once you finally get it, your guarenteed to not get another, because of this daily cooldown. And you need 6+ orbs to craft a weapon up to 5*.  And it's only for a single item. A single item, to show for all that pain and suffering you went through to get this. But as someone who chose a role, and stuck with it, this was never THAT big of a problem, but as I made alternate characters, or wanted to switch a role for my main character, (From Gunner to Bomber for example) I woud just give up, because with the armor and weapons, all to 4* or higher, you would need more than 15+ orbs. I'm just like, nope, ♥♥♥♥ that shizz, ain't worth it.
Crown/Currency inflation: There isn't really much to say here. It's your usual gold inflation you see in video games, but 10x WORSE. I remember bidding on my first Cailbur sword, and being so happy when I received that letter, saying I won. It was onlt about 800-1k crowns. One of my happiest experiences. I'll never forget it.  But as i'm typing this, a Calibur is worth 5-8k crowns. For a 2*/5* sword. It's ridiculous. Of course, theres no way to fix price inflation in video games. It's just a common thing. Still makes me sad though...
Finally, No Updates: It's what the title says. Look on every update, social media page, nothing. When the gunner update came out, it brought my faith back into the game. Then, nothing. People thought: "We got Sword update, the Gunner update, is the Bomber update next?!" To this day, nothing in terms of big updates. Or even small ones for that matter. Only bug fixes and yearly events. Of course, other things happened like a new company taking over, ect; but I wont get into that.
In conclusion: This is one of those games that I will always cherish. It paved the road for me as one of my favorite games. And yes, I do return to the game sometimes to see whats up, but nothing too extravagant. I just....can't get back into it though...It's clear the developers don't care about this beautiful game anymore. And although they did conclude the big question, "What happened to the squad inside the core?" they treated it as if they finished the game that still had a big community. But now, more than 50% of the community has left, no updates have come out, and everything is just....Old...
If you are reading this post, considering whether to download the game or not, please, please, PLEASE, download it. You will meet wonderful people, have a great experience with this game's story, and gameplay. Fun fact, I met one of my best friends, who I talk with on a daily basis, through this game. I'm grateful for every happy moment I had with this game. And it will forever be known as one of the best games I have ever played, despite it's very big flaws.. Play this game. You will not regret it. Thank you for reading this post to the end. <3

I wish I could give this a thumbs up and a thumbs down...
This game is not a traditional RPG if that's what you are looking for. There are some elements... but they matter VERY LITTLE.  The only thing that really matters is button mashing and flipping around mobs to avoid getting hit... because if you do get hit a few times... you're dead. You will die... again, and again, and again. There are fires that you can respawn at as checkpoints.
What is this game imo? This game is a console game for kids with ADD. You know the ones... the ones that give great RPGs really bad reviews because they are too easy and to short...because they try to run through the entire game without reading any dialouge or doing any side quests. Then they ♥♥♥♥♥ about how the game took 20 hours instead of the 60 as advertised. This game is for them. Why? The game cheats. It makes sure you die over and over and over. Impossible mechanics to survive your first time at a boss. It doesn't matter how well you know the character or it's limitations... unless you get very very lucky... you will die.
That is what this game is about in a nutshell. I wondered how the hell people put 9,000 hours in this game... guess no further... so many restarts it's absurd... and some people think this is fun... to each their own I guess. There is no relaxing moment to enjoy the scenery (which isn't bad) and after playing for 5 or 6 hours your shoulders will feel like rocks from playing this stressful game.
Yes, the world is a great concept. Yes, the mobs are pretty cool. The basic idea is great. The one difficulty level makes it absurd... not impossible... but not enjoyable if you want a good challenge but not one that makes you want to rip your hair out after a while.
The story...pff there is no real story that I have noticed... if you're expecting some detailed cool story... forget about it.

A lot of the negative reviews on this game concern the "grindy" nature of the game and the difficulty it brings to the table. I can see how in some ways this can be annoying but I think it only really ruins the game if one approaches Darkest Dungeon as the type of game you want to burn through and be done with in 20-30 hours. For myself, that is not the game I want to play nor is Darkest Dungeon that sort of game. The game even warns you before you make it to the main menu that the premise is about risk management and making hard choices. There aren't very many easy choices in the game and that is part of the allure; nearly every choice you make has some sort of advantage and an equally troubling drawback. I think that is what gives the game its charm. At the end of the day all the playable characters are simply human beings. They aren't superheroes or mystical badasses. They should die easily when faced with some of the eldritch horrors you deal with along the way. The game is certainly true to its form which is what makes succeeding on a particularly difficult boss that has killed a party or two so satisfying. If a difficult, risk manage-y game is not something you think you are into, I wouldn't get Darkest Dungeon. Overall, the game is gorgeous, great voice-acting and soundtrack and smooth gameplay. Like many here have said, if you aren't into the form of the game, it probably won't entertain.

PROS
* random map generation (the maps are quite detailed and can flow quite nicely)
* graphics are noticably better IMO.
* mag-weapons are cool looking and cool sounding
* loot items to improve weapons are cool.
* timed loot drops are a fun mechanic.
* sequential, one-at-a-time overwatch implementation (you don't waste them all on one dead target).
* you can fall from destroyed floors.
* GREMLINs! (little robots that extend the abilities of the Specialist)
* the Faceless are cool enemies.
* ADVENT are cool enemies (kind of like EXALT).
* experimental projects are cool (although the text is a bit heavy).
* you can use swords (Rangers).
* strategy layer is opened ended.
* ADVENT burger running gag is funny.
* Hacking is a fun diversion.
* game models are great!
* psi-op classes are amazing and very powerful.
CONS OR MIXED POINTS
* random map generation (timers can make them more a chore than fun).
* mag-weapons are just reskinned lasers and function as basic tier 2 weapons.
* would liked to have seen mag and laser weapons competing as a mid-tier weapons with their own perks and drawbacks.
* would have preferred to have loot add-ons as buildable en masse once retrieved and researched.
* over-reliance on destroying floors as a tactic--it seems all explosives destroy the floor totally.
* Supports are not as effective healers as they once were--they feel generic.
* still can't pick up your own dropped equipment in the field.
* viper enemies look stupid to me (breasts on a human-snake creature seems wrong).
* viper enemies have incredibly stupid range on their tongue grab (did they add frog DNA too?).
* stacking shield-bearers (different class shield bearers can stack; not sure if a bug or feature).
* random maps and timers some times work in your favor, some times make a stealth mission a marathon.
* swords are really special use despite their special high-tech blade types.
* swords don't seem to do high damage.
* determining where your Ranger ends up is not explained but this was fixed for me by a mod.
* strategy layer seems to be meandering--it's without structure and feels more like "honey-dos".
* story is uninteresting (to me).
--> EDIT: although the end game really picks the story up, but the start was boring.
* timed missions that run out of time are instant-over.
--> EDIT: I fixed this through mods.
* Central Officer Bradford is annoying at times ("We're running out of time Commander!").
* hacking success levels seem to be totally random.
* hackingrewards seem random; it feels more like gambling rather than strategy.
* no obvious replacement to the F1 info screen from XCOM1
--> EDIT: tooltips replace this functionality but I miss the info screen.
UPDATES AFTER FINISHING THE GAME
* most of the annoyances I have were fixed by the following mods:
--> Disable Timers; timers never tick-down, it allows you to counter bad situations elegantly
--> Stop Wasting My Time; built-in dramatic pauses removed; game feels more responsive
--> Instant Avenger Menus; no longer do you have to see transition effects for the 30,000th time
--> Slow Avatar; gives you more breathing room on Avatar project.
~> Also one of these mods also gave me the ability to pick where I end up when using Rangers
* Sectopods went from been unfairly hard in XCOM1 to just stupid in XCOM2; they do tremendous amounts of damage still but they walk janky and often have issues when animating their movement--it really brings you out of the game.
* Turrets are a realistic addition to the game
* The "set piece" missions of the game are AWESOME (The Forge, The ADVENT Tower, the Final Mission)
SUMMARY: with these mods the game went from a "don't buy" to a "buy when on sale". overall the game is not bad, but it just feels off. XCOM2 is a decent game (when modded) but to me, XCOM1 is still the superior game.

Starbound is a fantastic take on the sandbox survival genre. While still early-access, the game feels more like a finished product than most. With an immense and diverse game world, the game really immerses you and rewards you for exploration and buildilng, while not feeling like it's punishing you for playing it your way. The art style is charming, the controls work great, and combat feels fresh with randomized baddies with equally randomized abilities, meaning you'll never feel like you're fighting the same mobs over and over (a gripe I had with Minecraft). The crafting is simple yet rewarding, and the amount of customization in style is pretty overwhelming once you realize how much there is in the game. Multiplayer works as advertised (I've only hosted LAN games), but I never felt like I was competing for resources with my fellow players. There are elements to game that feel like they may be missing or could be improved upon, but Starbound is supported by a fantastic community that the developers are actively engaged with, and have always appeared open to feedback from those playing the game.
With a reasonable early access price tag, this is a game you don't want to miss out on!

I have never written a review for any game before, but I felt that this one was definitely worth my time and effort. That being said, here's my review...
I liked Terraria, and I played it relentlessly until I got all the stuff I wanted and then sorta lost interest. Starbound seems to be full of endless possibilities, and it's only in the beta state! I can't wait for the next update to this game so I can explore farther reaches of the universe and take on new bosses to be able to craft all new sorts of stuff!! Minecraft and Terraria couldn't really nail that for me. Although sometimes it gets frustrating with the amount of Pixels (in-game currency) lost for each death. I had 5800, died and was left with 3200. That death toll is slightly exorbidant. Something I would HIGHLY recommend is, the second you get into a new sector, get the required materials for the new armors set(s) unlocked at the crafting table. It will save you grief. Also carry a tent to sleep in when your health is low. I would recommend getting on with the Early Access so:
A: You can support the development so we recieve the best possible final product.
B: You get to enjoy the game right now, and every update from here on is like christmas and makes you go "ooh! new stuff!"
C: You don't have to pay the full release price, that I'm guessing will be about $25.00. So that saves you $10 and you get to enjoy a great game right now!

There are a lot of things about this game that bug the crap out of me. The timed missions, the Avatar project which basically puts a timer on the campaign itself, the scarcity of elerium cores which makes outfitting your squad kind of hard, the same old six person squad size, the needless delays that make the game seem to grind to a halt at the worst possible times...the list goes on and on...
But there is a mod for every one of those complaints. Every. Single. One.
For everything about this game I din't like, someone else didn't like it either and made a mod to fix it. Then all of these truly amazing modders came along and created wonderful content that took an already impressively open game and expanded it even further. I have no idea how many mods I am currently subscribed to at this point, but every complaint I had about the game when I first bought it has been addressed by the community and my games are much more diverse due to all of the options unlocked through user created content. I'd also like to add that despite having an absurd number of mods active the game is VERY stable. This many mods on something like Fallout New Vegas? Forget about it.
So if you enjoyed XCOM and were on the fence about this one you should consider giving it a try. If there is something you heard about it that made you hesitant about picking it up, wait for it to go on sale. I am glad I bought it, though, and it is even better than the previous iteration.

So, starbound, an early access game that I thought of as being "Terraria in space." I had played terraria a lot with friends before buying this game and loved terraria, so I assumed that this would be the next terraria. A friend of mine had bought the game and I had watched him play it a bit, everything looked awesome, from the tools he had to the things he did, I was convinced. I bought this game at its full price at the time, which was 15 dollars and started to install and play. The gameplay seemed odd and clunky and unfinished, but i convinced myself it was fine and played on with my friends. I then put the game down for probably 4 months. I finally started playing again around may.
Ok now on to my opinion now
I came back to the game thinking it would be completely different in terms of new content, being away from and still growing game for 4 month you would expect that. I found the game nearly identical to how it last was, it felt odd and unfinished. Me and another friend had the same feeling towards the game and compared it to terraria. Now terraria has a fun, not very complicated feel to it, you can get into the game in minutes. Now starbound on the other hand I had a hard time getting used to, I knew about the game and how to play, just playing it wasn't enjoyable.
I'm not sure how to explain it but it just was not fun to play at its current state, it was odd, seemingly unfinished and just overall weird. Because of that I can not recommend this game at its current state.
Edit: So I wanna add some things that I forgot. This game has some potential, If we get updates more and with more content this game could live up to its "Terraria in space" image. I think this game could be salvaged but I feel due to the amount of negetive reviews, they have lost most of their current player base, unless it is slavaged, they lost me as well.

A lot of the negative reviews on this game concern the "grindy" nature of the game and the difficulty it brings to the table. I can see how in some ways this can be annoying but I think it only really ruins the game if one approaches Darkest Dungeon as the type of game you want to burn through and be done with in 20-30 hours. For myself, that is not the game I want to play nor is Darkest Dungeon that sort of game. The game even warns you before you make it to the main menu that the premise is about risk management and making hard choices. There aren't very many easy choices in the game and that is part of the allure; nearly every choice you make has some sort of advantage and an equally troubling drawback. I think that is what gives the game its charm. At the end of the day all the playable characters are simply human beings. They aren't superheroes or mystical badasses. They should die easily when faced with some of the eldritch horrors you deal with along the way. The game is certainly true to its form which is what makes succeeding on a particularly difficult boss that has killed a party or two so satisfying. If a difficult, risk manage-y game is not something you think you are into, I wouldn't get Darkest Dungeon. Overall, the game is gorgeous, great voice-acting and soundtrack and smooth gameplay. Like many here have said, if you aren't into the form of the game, it probably won't entertain.

Its Age of Empires. Come on. What more could you want?
Admittedly, it is a lot different from the first 2 Age of Empires that were developed by ensemble, which did have their own special charm. Age of Empires 3 feels different, but once you get into it you can completely tell that they're one of the same. I love this game for many reasons. You can play a little of each civilization and choose which is your favorite. They all have a different playstyle and personally my favorite is the Ottomans because of their free villagers. I also like them because their units look incredibly Bad A- in a formation. 50 Janissaries. 25 abus guns, some gardeners and great bombards marching toward the enemy base is a sight to behold.
Anyways, if you've played any of the past Age of Empires games and enjoyed them, or just plain love strategy or war games, then please for the sake of all that is good - get this game. I would advise you to go into this experience with a friend. Yes, single player skirmish does get a little stale. With a friend however, it becomes a LOT more fun.
Some things that I LIKE about this game:
Home city cards (Come on, who doesnt love these?)
Civilization bonuses (Much more variety compared to Age of Empires 2)
Unique units (Units that arent a copy+paste like the common musketeer)
Trading posts (Hell yes.. upgrade to train and you're in business baby... just remember to defend them)
The music (Seriously, go check it out yourself. I hum along to the menu theme a lot)
Tons of mods ( Ill talk about that later)
Some things that I DONT like about this game:
They've removed the "patrol" option that everyone loved in Age of Empires 2
You cant rotate buildings
AI gets a little stupid now and then. (Mortar ships trying to fire at shore and cant find a "comfortable" position to fire from)
Getting the game to run for some systems has been troublesome.
Mercenaries (In my opinion, they could have spent more time developing more unique units for every civilization rather than these. I rarely ever use them.)
Wood is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥(If i ever have economy problems, its always because theres a shortage of wood)
The Japanese are a tad overpowered. (Not only in military but in my opinion they have incredible advantages in economy as well)
Most of the things I dont like in the game are actually solved with some mods, in particular, the Improvement mod by Mandos. I can't begin to address how much that mod makes a great game into a spectacular game. Things such as improved AI. Theres also little things like adding your civilizatons icon to your ship's sails (Love that) and even damage being dealt to units who get run over by the trade route caravan. (You didnt think you could get away with a train running you over, did you?). Theres an entire page of improvements in this mod and none of them are detrimental to the gameplay at all, in my opinion. If you dont like it, you can just uninstall it.
This mod isnt at all necessary for this game to be great on its own, however.
It's old, but its fantastic. The campaign story is great, and you get the war chiefs and asian dynasties to go with the original. If you're considering buying this game, look no further.
